mcqs.question: What is the definition of a crystal lattice?

options.A: A regular arrangement of atoms, ions or molecules in a repeating pattern extending in three dimensions.
options.B: A single molecule isolated in space.
options.D: A two‑dimensional pattern on a surface.

mcqs.answer: A regular arrangement of atoms, ions or molecules in a repeating pattern extending in three dimensions.
mcqs.explanation: A crystal lattice is the three‑dimensional, periodic arrangement of constituent particles (atoms, ions, molecules) that repeats throughout the solid. Option A captures this definition; the other options describe isolated, random, or two‑dimensional arrangements, which are not lattices.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a unit cell in a crystal lattice?

options.A: The smallest repeating three‑dimensional portion of the lattice that, when stacked, recreates the whole crystal.
options.D: The surface layer of a crystal.

mcqs.answer: The smallest repeating three‑dimensional portion of the lattice that, when stacked, recreates the whole crystal.
mcqs.explanation: A unit cell is the smallest repeatable three‑dimensional building block of a crystal lattice; stacking it in three dimensions reproduces the entire crystal. Options B, C and D describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify primitive and centred unit cells
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a primitive unit cell from a centred unit cell?

options.A: A primitive cell contains only one lattice point per cell, whereas a centred cell has additional lattice points at its centre or faces.
options.B: A primitive cell is larger than a centred cell.
options.C: A centred cell has no lattice points at the corners.
options.D: Both have the same number of lattice points.

mcqs.answer: A primitive cell contains only one lattice point per cell, whereas a centred cell has additional lattice points at its centre or faces.
mcqs.explanation: In a primitive cell the net count of lattice points is one (corner points shared). A centred cell (body‑centred or face‑centred) adds extra points at the centre of the cell or on its faces, increasing the lattice point count. Hence option A is correct.

mcqs.question: In a face‑centered cubic (FCC) lattice, what is the coordination number of each ion?
mcqs.explanation: In an FCC arrangement each ion touches twelve nearest neighbours, giving a coordination number of 12. Options B, C and D correspond to other lattice types (BCC, simple cubic, etc.).

mcqs.question: Why does NaCl have a higher melting point than KCl?

options.A: NaCl has a higher lattice energy due to smaller ionic radii, leading to a higher melting point.
options.B: NaCl forms covalent bonds, which increase its melting point.
options.C: NaCl has a larger molecular weight than KCl.
options.D: NaCl crystals are more irregular in shape, causing a higher melting point.

mcqs.answer: NaCl has a higher lattice energy due to smaller ionic radii, leading to a higher melting point.
mcqs.explanation: Smaller Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions result in shorter inter‑ionic distances and stronger electrostatic attraction, i.e., higher lattice energy, which raises the melting point. Options B, C and D refer to unrelated factors.

mcqs.question: A student observes that a solid metal can be cut into identical small cubes that, when reassembled, reproduce the original shape without gaps. Which concept does this observation illustrate?
mcqs.explanation: The ability to fill space completely by repeating identical building blocks reflects a crystal lattice—a periodic three‑dimensional arrangement of particles. The other options describe non‑periodic or unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about a unit cell is incorrect?

options.A: A unit cell is the smallest repeating unit that can build up the entire crystal lattice.
options.B: A unit cell always contains a whole atom at each corner.
options.C: The dimensions of a unit cell are defined by the lattice parameters.
options.D: Unit cells can be primitive or centred.

mcqs.answer: A unit cell always contains a whole atom at each corner.
mcqs.explanation: Atoms at the corners are shared among adjacent cells; a unit cell does not need to contain whole atoms at each corner. Therefore statement B is false. The other statements correctly describe unit cells.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify primitive and centred unit cells
mcqs.question: If a cubic lattice has lattice points at each corner and one at the centre of the cube, what type of unit cell is it?
mcqs.explanation: A cubic cell with points at the eight corners plus one at the body centre is a body‑centred cubic (BCC) unit cell. Primitive cubic lacks the centre point, and face‑centred has points on each face. Hexagonal close packed is a different crystal system.
